episodes.title: Kept: Jeremiah 33-35, Ecclesiastes 10, John 4, 1 Peter 1
episodes.summary: Pilot episode, about ten minutes, built around the word 'kept.' Jeremiah 33: God's call to prayer from prison, the righteous Branch and the name 'The Lord is our righteousness,' and the covenant with David and Levi tied to day and night. Jeremiah 34: Zedekiah warned; the slave-release covenant broken once the siege lifted, the calf cut in two, contrasted with Genesis 15. Jeremiah 35: the Rechabites' obedience to Jonadab versus Judah's disobedience, and the promise that Jonadab will never lack a man to stand before God (not a teetotal mandate; Christian liberty). Ecclesiastes 10: dead flies, sharpening the dull iron (v. 10), the sagging roof, the bird that carries your words. John 4: the woman leaves her jar; shame turned to testimony; 'my food is to do the will of him who sent me.' 1 Peter 1:1-9: elect exiles, living hope, an inheritance kept and believers guarded, faith tested like gold.
threads: Jeremiah 35 was covered only briefly; the next Jeremiah episode can deepen it and then move into Jeremiah 36-38 (the scroll burned, Jeremiah in the cistern).
The 'never lack a man' promises link Jeremiah 33:17-18 and 35:19.
Ecclesiastes is heading toward its close in chapters 11-12.
1 Peter's theme of exile and the scattered people of God echoes Jeremiah's exile setting.

The pilot leaned on New Testament fulfillment in every section; the listener asked for future episodes to stay in each passage and its commentary, using the New Testament only where the text warrants.

Jeremiah 33-35, Ecclesiastes 10, John 4:27-34, 1 Peter 1:1-9

episodes.title: Torn Scroll, Untorn Robes: Jeremiah 35-38, Ecclesiastes 11, John 4, 1 Peter 1
episodes.summary: Jeremiah 35-38 was taught around the verb shama, to hear and obey: the book is arranged by message, not calendar (Calvin), so the Rechabites who obey a dead ancestor (35) are set beside Jehoiakim burning the scroll (36), then Zedekiah under siege (37-38). On 35 the episode used Calvin on God 'rising early' (Hebrew shakam), Calvin and Gill on 'stand before me' as family survival and household worship rather than priesthood, and Jerome's Letter 58 claiming the Rechabites for monasticism, with Calvin's rejection of binding rules drawn from the chapter. On 36 it dated the scroll to 605 B.C. and the reading to Kislev 604 (the month Babylon destroyed Ashkelon), noted the Gemaryahu son of Shaphan bulla and the Shaphan-Josiah link, explained the kara/kara wordplay (read/tear) with Henry on Josiah tearing his robes, and answered the 36:30 difficulty about Jehoiachin with Gill and Poole. On 37-38 it covered Zedekiah's secret 'Is there any word from the Lord?' (Calvin: he wanted a new word), the Jehucal and Gedaliah bullae, Spurgeon's 1890 sermon 'Zedekiah, or the Man Who Cannot Say No,' the cistern and the verb 'sank' echoed in 38:22, Ebed-melech with Begg's ropes-and-rags line, and the hard question of Jeremiah's partial answer in 38:24-27 (Calvin uneasy; Henry, Poole, Gill defend; Larger Catechism on the ninth commandment); application: stop waiting privately for a cheaper word than the one God already gave. Ecclesiastes 11 was taught as acting under four 'you do not know' statements, with Gregory Thaumaturgus and Spurgeon's 1890 sermon on 11:4, ruach as wind and spirit in 11:5, and 11:9 read as sincere joy under judgment with Gill against the irony reading of Henry, Poole, and Gregory. John 4:43-54 covered the 4:44 puzzle (Augustine, Chrysostom, Calvin following Cyril, Sproul's irony reading), the plural 'you' in 4:48, Chrysostom on healing the father's mind, Sproul's 'believing God,' Calvin and Spurgeon on growing faith, and Augustine's 'what signs have we seen?' 1 Peter 1:10-16 covered the prophets' search, the Spirit of Christ in the prophets (Henry; Clement of Alexandria's angel reading noted and rejected), Old Testament saints' salvation (Calvin; Westminster Confession 7.5), Calvin's 'they spread the table,' parakupto, Piper on hope as the letter's first command, and holiness from Leviticus with 'children of obedience' tied back to hearing.
threads: Jeremiah 39-43 is next: the fall of Jerusalem (39), Zedekiah's capture and blinding, Ebed-melech's promised reward (39:15-18) after his rescue of Jeremiah in 38, Jeremiah's release, Gedaliah's governorship and assassination, and the flight to Egypt.
Follow the shama (hear/obey) thread into 39-43, especially 42-43 where the remnant asks Jeremiah for a word and then refuses it, a repeat of Zedekiah's pattern.
Lamentations 3:55 was linked to the cistern; could be revisited when the plan reaches Lamentations.
Hegesippus's account (Eusebius, Church History 2.23) of a Rechabite priest at the death of James the Just was researched but not used; Gill doubts it.
Lachish Letters (Letter 4 on Azekah, compare Jeremiah 34:7; Letter 6 'slacken the hands,' compare 38:4) were researched but not used; available for 39 and the fall of Judah's towns.

Ecclesiastes 12 closes the book next: 'Remember also your Creator' continues 11:9-10; the aging poem and the epilogue 'fear God and keep his commandments.' The 11:9 irony-or-sincere question may come up again.
John 5:1-15 is next: the healing at the pool on the Sabbath, the third sign; contrast with the official who believed the word in 4:50.

1 Peter 1:17-25 is next: fear during the time of exile, ransomed by precious blood, born again through the living and abiding word (1:23-25 quotes Isaiah 40, a natural tie to the burned-and-rewritten scroll of Jeremiah 36).

Voices used this episode: Calvin (3 quotes), Jerome, Henry, Gill, Spurgeon (2), Begg, Gregory Thaumaturgus, Chrysostom, Augustine, Sproul, Piper. Next time consider Poole, Trapp, Ryle, Boice, Owen, or Watson for variety.
episodes.description:
John 4:43-54, 1 Peter 1:10-16, Ecclesiastes 11, Jeremiah 35-38

Jehoiakim cut Jeremiah's scroll column by column and burned it, yet no one in the room tore his robe. We go deeper into the Rechabites, then follow Jeremiah through the burned scroll, the dungeon, and the muddy cistern, and ask whether he lied to Zedekiah's officials. Also Ecclesiastes 11 on sowing without knowing, the official who believed Jesus' word in John 4, and the prophets who served us in 1 Peter 1.

episodes.title: Packed for Egypt: Jeremiah 39-43, Ecclesiastes 12, John 5, 1 Peter 1
episodes.summary: Jeremiah 39-43 carried the shama (hear/obey) thread to its end. Chapter 39 was taught as the book's hinge: the siege dated January 588 to July 586 B.C., Lachish Letter 4 (cannot see Azekah), the Nebo-Sarsekim tablet confirming 39:3, the Babylonian officers sitting in the gate as Jeremiah 1:15 foretold, and Zedekiah caught at Jericho and blinded at Riblah, which reconciles Jeremiah 34:3 with Ezekiel 12:13 (Henry: darkness for the man who shut his eyes to the word). Ebed-melech's promise (39:15-18) was explained through batach, trust, contrasted with Judah's false trust in Jeremiah 7 and 17 (Spurgeon's Faith's Checkbook; MacLaren: the object of faith is a Person; Calvin: unbelief is always timid). Nebuzaradan preaching 'you did not obey his voice' (Poole; Calvin) and Gedaliah of the family of Shaphan at Mizpah were covered, with the Lachish Gedaliah bulla, the summer-fruit harvest, Gedaliah's refusal to believe Johanan (Henry: the dove without the serpent; Calvin's middle path between gullibility and cruelty), his murder at table in the seventh month (Gill on the Fast of Gedaliah, Zechariah 7:5), the 80 pilgrims thrown into Asa's cistern, and the flight toward Egypt. The hard question of chapter 42 was the remnant's sincerity: their oath 'whether good or bad, we will obey' (Calvin: hearing and obeying the voice amount to the same), the ten days' wait (Henry, Calvin), the 'build and plant' offer echoing Jeremiah 1:10, 42:20 'gone astray against your souls', and Calvin's paragraph on asking counsel after the decision is made; 43 covered 'you are telling a lie' (Poole: deny it is God's will rather than defy God), the double 'did not obey the voice', Tahpanhes and Petrie's pavement, Nebuchadnezzar 'my servant' and the 568 B.C. campaign, and the stoning tradition (Tertullian, Jerome). Application: before asking God for guidance, ask whether you are willing for either answer. Ecclesiastes 12 covered the plural 'Creator' (Henry, Gill), the three 'befores', the aging house poem read loosely, the almond (Gill, linked to Jeremiah 1:11-12 shaqed/shoqed), 12:7 reversing Genesis 2, Henry's 'cream and flower' line, goads and nails, and 12:13 'the whole of man' with Augustine's City of God 20.3. John 5:1-15 covered the unnamed feast, the excavated five porticoes against skeptics and Augustine's five-books allegory, the missing verse 4 (Piper), Spurgeon's 1870 sermon on the paralyzed will ('breakfast with the devil, and sup with Christ'), Chrysostom on 38 years versus ten days of prayer, Calvin's citation of Jeremiah 17:21 for the Sabbath burden, 'sin no more' (Piper: holiness, not health), and the ambiguous 5:15. 1 Peter 1:17-25 covered paroikia exile set against the remnant's refusal to live under Babylon, God judging the heart (Calvin), lutroo and mataios, Calvin's 'ruinous labyrinth of wanderings', Gregory Nazianzen on to whom the ransom was paid, Polycarp's echo of 1:13 and 1:21, unhypocritical love, Isaiah 40, and Piper on imperishability and the infinite value of Christ's blood.
threads: Jeremiah 44-46 is next: Jeremiah's last sermon to the Judeans in Egypt and the queen of heaven (44), the word to Baruch (45), and the start of the oracles against the nations with Egypt and Carchemish (46). The 568 B.C. invasion of Egypt mentioned today bears on 44:30 and 46.
The shama (hear/obey) thread climaxed in 42:6 versus 43:4 and 43:7; chapter 44 continues it with the people's open refusal ('we will not listen to you'). Close the thread there.
The stoning tradition for Jeremiah in Egypt (Tertullian, Scorpiace 8; Jerome, Against Jovinianus 2.37) was mentioned; the Lives of the Prophets places it at Tahpanhes, not yet verified.
The Baruch accusation in 43:3 sets up chapter 45.
The almond/watching wordplay (Jeremiah 1:11-12) was introduced; can be recalled when the book closes.

Ecclesiastes is finished; Song of Songs begins tomorrow and needs a book introduction (authorship, the allegorical and literal readings, Bernard of Clairvaux and the Puritans; Calvin wrote no commentary on it).

John 5:16-30 is next: Jesus's defense, 'My Father is working until now, and I am working', equality with the Father, and the two resurrections of 5:24-29 (already pointed to from 5:14 today). Calvin on 5:17 on the Sabbath and God's continuing providence is in the research file.
1 Peter 2:1-8 is next: long for the pure spiritual milk, the living stone, the spiritual house; 'therefore' ties back to the new birth through the word in 1:23-25.

Voices used this episode: Henry (2), Calvin (2 quoted, several paraphrased), Poole (2), Spurgeon (2), MacLaren, Jerome, Augustine, Chrysostom, Polycarp, Piper. Sproul did not have accessible material on these passages. Next time consider Sproul, Ryle, Boice, Owen, Bernard of Clairvaux (Song of Songs), Leighton on 1 Peter, Gill.
episodes.description:
John 5:1-15, 1 Peter 1:17-25, Ecclesiastes 12, Jeremiah 39-43

Jerusalem falls, Zedekiah is blinded, and an Ethiopian who trusted God walks out alive. Then the survivors swear to obey whatever God says, wait ten days for the answer, and go to Egypt anyway. Also: the end of Ecclesiastes, the man at the pool of Bethesda, and the imperishable word in 1 Peter.

episodes.title: Whose Word Will Stand: Jeremiah 44-46, Song of Songs 1, John 5, 1 Peter 2
episodes.summary: Jeremiah 44-46 closed the shama (hear/obey) thread: Jeremiah's last recorded sermon to Judeans scattered across Egypt (Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, Pathros), the queen of heaven cult (Ishtar/Astarte, cakes, household religion from Jeremiah 7:18), and the participle 'we are not listening to you' (44:16) as the end of a ladder from Jehoiakim's knife to open refusal, with Poole ('now these women and men rise higher') and Calvin ('God will not and cannot have himself separated from his word'). The hard question was the argument from experience in 44:17-18 (Josiah's reform in 622, Megiddo in 609), answered by 44:21-23 and 2 Kings 23:26 (delayed judgment for Manasseh), Calvin on patience, and Augustine's City of God ('Drought and Christianity go hand in hand', plus the Carthage goddess Caelestis that Gill links to the queen of heaven); the application was to let God's word interpret circumstances rather than the reverse. It also covered qum ('make your vows stand' versus 'whose word will stand', 44:25-29), shoqed in 44:27 recalling the almond of 1:12, the Hophra sign (Herodotus on Apries), and chapter 45 as a hinge dated 605 between 45:1 and 46:2, with the views on Baruch's 'great things' (Calvin, Gill, Jewish tradition, Poole), Calvin on faltering mid-course, Henry's 'painting thy own cabin', and Spurgeon's Midsummer Common story; chapter 46 covered Carchemish (Babylonian Chronicle), 46:17 'Noisy one' as a pun on Hophra, and 46:27-28 'not a full end' with Calvin on election and his living-root image. Song of Songs got its introduction (superlative title, Solomon, Akiva's 'holy of holies', Passover, Origen, Bernard, Durham and Sibbes, the modern literal reading), the episode's position (plain sense first, quoting Sproul via Ligonier, then Ephesians 5:32 marriage typology with restraint), and chapter 1: 'draw me, let us run', 1:5-6 as sunburn and the unkept vineyard (Spurgeon's warning to church workers), and mutual praise in 1:15-16. John 5:16-30 covered God's continuing work after Genesis 2:2 (Philo, Calvin), Chrysostom's argument that the defense only works if the Son is equal, Augustine's 'the Jews understand what the Arians do not', 5:19 as unity of work (Calvin's Mediator reading noted), Ryle on the presentness of salvation in 5:24, the two resurrections of 5:25 and 5:28, and Calvin on works as mark not cause in 5:29. 1 Peter 2:1-8 covered dolos/adolos and logikos (Calvin versus his editor), Piper on growing by the word and 'a new taste', milk as lifelong appetite, Clement's 'the Lord is Christ', Peter's name and the living stones, the priesthood of believers alongside ordained ministry (Larger Catechism 158), Calvin's 'build on him, or be dashed against him', and Leighton declining to speculate on 2:8.
threads: Jeremiah 47-48 is next: oracles against the Philistines (47) and Moab (48). The oracles against the nations run through chapter 51; Egypt (46) was first. Chapter 46:13-26 looked ahead to Nebuchadnezzar's 568/567 invasion of Egypt (BM 33041).
The shama (hear/obey) thread is now closed (44:16 'we are not listening'); a new thread could be qum, 'stand', which tied 44:25-29 together ('whose word will stand').
The 'great' (gadol) thread was mentioned briefly: 44:7 great evil, 44:26 great name, 45:5 great things, 33:3 great and hidden things.
Baruch's role as possible compiler of the book, and his family (brother Seraiah, 51:59), can return when the plan reaches Jeremiah 51.
The fate of Jeremiah after Jeremiah 44 is unrecorded; the stoning tradition was mentioned in episode 3. Jeremiah 52 is a historical appendix.

Song of Songs 2 is next: the lily among brambles, the banqueting house, the refrain 'do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases' (2:7), and the spring invitation (2:8-17). The interpretive position (plain sense first, Christ and the church through Ephesians 5 without pressing details) should be kept consistent. Voices available: Bernard, Durham, Sibbes, Henry, Gill, Spurgeon, Hudson Taylor, Duguid (secondhand only).
John 5:31-47 is next: the four witnesses (John the Baptist, the works, the Father, the Scriptures), 'you search the Scriptures' and 'Moses wrote of me'.

1 Peter 2:9-17 is next: chosen race, royal priesthood (Exodus 19:6), 'once you were not a people' (Hosea), sojourners and exiles abstaining from passions, submission to every human institution. The priesthood of believers was introduced today from 2:5; 2:9 completes it.

Voices used this episode: Calvin (3 quoted, several paraphrased), Poole, Augustine (2), Henry, Spurgeon (2), Sproul via Ligonier, Chrysostom, Ryle, Piper, Leighton. Desiring God blocked fetches; the Piper quotes came from a Gospel Translations transcript. Next time consider Owen, Watson, Boice, Bernard, Durham, Gill, MacLaren, Hilary, or Cyril of Alexandria.
episodes.description:
John 5:16-30, 1 Peter 2:1-8, Song of Songs 1, Jeremiah 44-46

Jeremiah's last sermon meets an open refusal in Egypt, God answers with 'whose word will stand, mine or theirs?', and Baruch is told not to seek great things for himself. The Song of Songs begins, Jesus claims the Father's work and the Father's honor in John 5, and Peter calls newborn believers to crave the word and come to the Living Stone.
